## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.

When an integration uses `async_generate_entity_id()` to create a new entity id, it passes a `suggested_object_id` (string).

If this string too long, a `MaxLengthExceeded` exception is raised.  This is all ok. However if a `suggested_object_id` comes from user content (e.g. from a slugified URL or some other long unique identifier), it could be very long.  It's also possible that the incrementing suffix to avoid duplicates could tip it over the edge.

Rather than limit the length at all of the sources, I thought that it *might* be better to auto-truncate strings in `async_generate_entity_id()`

This PR does this and fixes the related issue I found.  But I would value a 2nd opinion as this is not the only way to solve it.

For example are there any scenarios where it would be more helpful to raise an exception?  If that is the case `auto_truncate` could maybe be added as an optional parameter.  But only if that complexity is worth it.

issue_context.title: Generic Camera - MaxLengthExceeded
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I have a generic camera with templates in the still_image_url.
This is the one that is not automatically imported.
If i try to set it up manually the MaxLengthExceeded Exception is raised.
For me it looks like the integration sets the name of the camera from the still_image_url, and that is too long.

I think a `name` option for the camera like in the yaml configuration would be helpfull. 

EDIT: After renaming the entity_id in the UI Config, the camera works as expected.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2022.4.0b4

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

core-2022.3.8

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Core

### Integration causing the issue

Generic Camera

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://rc.home-assistant.io/integrations/generic

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
# ISS
- platform: generic
  name: ISS
  still_image_url: http://static-maps.yandex.ru/1.x/?lang=en-US&ll={{ states.binary_sensor.iss.attributes.long }},{{ states.binary_sensor.iss.attributes.lat }}&size=650,450&z=3&l=sat,skl&pt=9.955727,49.821417,flag~-49.94082957,41.72583043,flag~{{ states.binary_sensor.iss.attributes.long }},{{ states.binary_sensor.iss.attributes.lat }},pmyws
  limit_refetch_to_url_change: true
```

@VDRainer I think there are two issues that you have raised.

If I understand correctly, the first issue is that templates in URLs can result in errors/warnings during startup if the corresponding entities aren't ready yet.  The issue makes sense but I can't see how it would be a new problem.  If it is definitely occurring in isolation please could you raise it as a separate issue?

If I understand correctly, the second is that long URLs generate a MaxLengthExceeded error.  We can discuss that issue here.

I have been able to reproduce this in a test case here:
https://github.com/davet2001/home-assistant/tree/generic_still_image_long_url

But this would appear to be something that can affect any entity id.  The error can be reproduced without using templates.

I have a solution which is to truncate the entity id string in entity_registry.py:292, i.e. changing
```
        test_string = preferred_string
```
to
```
        test_string = preferred_string[: MAX_LENGTH_STATE_ENTITY_ID - 3]
```

That means you would always have a few characters spare to iterate with if necessary.

Would highly value one of the core dev's opinion on this.

I think this issue will be fixed with your proposed solution.
Maybe it makes sence to mention in the release notes that auto import YAML can fail if there are templates in the still_image_url with entitys not ready on startup?

> Maybe it makes sence to mention in the release notes that auto import YAML can fail if there are templates in the still_image_url with entitys not ready on startup?
